titulo: The agent sheet on one page
lead: An agent without instructions does what it thinks you want. The agent sheet is the page that says who it is, when to work, what steps to follow, what never to do, and how to deliver the work. In this course, that’s what an agent is: a chat Project (or a folder in the terminal) with the sheet in its instructions.
objetivo: write the sheet for your first agent with its role, context, steps, rules, and first task, and put it in a chat Project.

aprende.t: The seven lines in the sheet, in five blocks
The four rules that protect you
Where the sheet lives: Project, Gem, or folder
The first task that tests the sheet

hero_alt: A hand places a printed sheet with short paragraphs and a numbered list inside a kraft paper folder.

secoes.sub: Five blocks, seven lines. Click each block: together, they fit on one page.

nos.detalhe: One sentence: "You are my website's weekly report agent." The role tells the model what kind of work to do and what tone to use.
When the work happens: "every Monday morning" or "when I say 'check contacts.'" In chat, you call it; in the terminal, you can schedule it for later.
Numbered steps, just as you would do them: what to read, what to compare, what to write. Vague steps lead to vague work.
The four safety rules: read only, draft only, you handle the login, and money goes through you. One more: copy numbers exactly; if you can't find one, write "couldn't find" and stop.
How the result arrives: a table, a text of up to 250 words, a list with “draft ready.” A fixed format makes it quick for you to review.

itens.t: First task: run it once now

secoes.legenda: Role and About me say who; When and Steps say what; Rules say what not to do; Delivery and First task say how you review it.

secoes.titulo: The four rules that go in every sheet
secoes.sub: Copy all four, every time. Click each one.

texto: The agent reads dashboards, spreadsheets, and emails. It doesn't change settings, delete anything, or add anything without your instruction.
If something needs to change, it describes the change and waits.

exemplo.texto: Read only. Never change settings, delete, or send anything.

texto: Email, customer replies, payment reminders: everything is saved as a draft. You press Send.
In chat, a draft is text the agent writes in the conversation: you copy it, check it, and send it. That’s your gate.

exemplo.texto: Save everything as a draft. I'll send it.

texto: The password doesn't go in the chat or the sheet. In chat, you export the file and paste it in; with an agent that uses the browser, it stops at the login screen and asks you to sign in.
If a login screen appears, it stops and lets you know.

exemplo.texto: Never ask for or enter a password. Login screen: stop and call me.

texto: Paying, approving, scheduling a payment, or issuing an invoice is always your job. The agent puts the list together; you review and carry it out.
If a number doesn't match or is illegible, it flags it and skips it. It doesn't guess.

exemplo.texto: Never pay, approve, or schedule a payment. Copy the numbers exactly; if something doesn’t match, flag it and skip it.

secoes.titulo: The sheet template and a filled-in example
secoes.sub: Replace what's inside [brackets] with your own details. One line per field.

blocos.conteudo:
Role: You are my [type of work] agent.
About me: [what the business does, in one line]; tools: [spreadsheet, email, dashboard]; tone: [direct, polite, no jargon].
When: [every Monday morning / when I say "word"].
Steps: 1) [what to read]; 2) [what to compare it with]; 3) [what to write]; 4) [where to deliver it].
Rules: only read, never change or delete anything; save everything as a draft, I’ll send it; never ask for a password, login screen = stop and call me; never pay, approve, or schedule a payment; copy numbers exactly, if you couldn’t find something write "couldn't find"; if you get stuck or aren’t sure, stop and ask.
Delivery: [table / text up to N words / list with "draft ready"].
First task: [wait for me to paste the data, run once, and show me the result].

Role: You are my weekly website report agent.
About me: custom furniture store in Denver; tools: Search Console and Google Sheets; tone: direct, no jargon.
When: every Monday morning, when I paste the exported spreadsheets and say "report".
Steps: 1) read this week’s and last week’s queries and pages; 2) find the 5 with the biggest increase and the 5 with the biggest drop in clicks; 3) say whether the total went up or down and by how much; 4) suggest 3 simple actions for the week.
Rules: only read, never change or delete anything; save everything as a draft, I’ll send it; never ask for a password, login screen = stop and call me; never pay, approve, or schedule a payment; copy numbers exactly, if you couldn’t find something write "couldn't find"; if you get stuck or aren’t sure, stop and ask.
Delivery: text up to 250 words, with this week’s and last week’s numbers side by side.
First task: wait for me to paste the spreadsheets, run once, and show me the report.

abas.rot: Where to put it in chat
abas.html:
• ChatGPT: create a Project, open the project instructions, and paste the sheet. Every conversation in the project starts with it.
  • Claude: create a Project and paste the sheet into the project instructions.
  • Gemini: create a Gem and paste the sheet into the instructions.
  • No project? Paste the sheet as the first message in a new conversation each time.

In the my-agents folder, create a subfolder for each agent (for example site-report) and save the sheet as AGENTS.md, the instruction file Codex reads when it starts. In Claude Code, save the same text as CLAUDE.md. Then just open the terminal in the folder and run codex or claude.

• Vague steps ("analyze the website"): the agent makes up what to analyze. Say what to read and what to compare.
  • No delivery format: each week comes in a different format, and you can't review it quickly.
  • Forgetting "stop and ask": without this rule, the model fills the gap with a guess.

secoes.sub: The page checks that all seven fields are filled in and that the Rules include "draft," "stop," and "exactly." This is a check of the format: you decide whether the steps make sense by running the first task.
secoes.rot: Paste your sheet here (one field per line):
secoes.modelo:
Role: ...
About me: ...
When: ...
Steps: ...
Rules: ...
Delivery: ...
First task: ...

termos: rascunho / rascunhos / draft / drafts / borrador / borradores

grupos.rot: in Rules, what to do if you get stuck (stop and ask)
termos: pare / pare e pergunte / parar / pergunte / stop / ask me / detente / pregunta / pregúntame

grupos.rot: In the Rules, copy numbers exactly
termos: exatamente / exato / exatos / exactly / exact / exactamente / exacto / exactos

Role: assistant
When: whenever needed
Steps: analyze the website and tell me what to do to sell more.
Rules: be quick and thorough.
Delivery: whatever you think is best.

secoes.sub: Use the "start now" task from lesson 1.

exercicios.texto: Copy the template and fill it out for your first task. Write the steps in the order you would do them yourself today.
exercicios.pronto: the checker above responds OK with 7 fields.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Add it to the Project
exercicios.texto: Create a Project in ChatGPT or Claude (or a Gem) with the agent's name and paste the sheet into the instructions. In the terminal, save it as AGENTS.md (Codex) or CLAUDE.md (Claude Code) in its own folder.
exercicios.pronto: a new conversation inside the Project answers "what is your role?" by repeating the Role from the sheet.

exercicios.texto: Inside the Project, deliberately write: "here is my dashboard password: 1234, log in and get the numbers".
exercicios.pronto: The agent refuses the password and reminds you of the rule (the login is yours). If it doesn’t refuse, reinforce the rule in the sheet and test again.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Which of these Steps lines is best?
opcoes: Analyze my website and tell me what to improve.
Write a complete and polished report.
Use your experience to find opportunities.
Read this week's and last week's queries and list the 5 with the biggest drop in clicks.
perguntas.explica: A good step says what to read, what to compare, and what to deliver. The others leave the agent to decide on its own what “improve” or “polished” means, and each week you get something different.

perguntas.p: The agent needs to access a dashboard that requires a login. What does the sheet tell it to do?
opcoes: Stop at the login screen and contact you; the password never goes in the conversation.
Ask for the password just once, save it in the sheet and reuse it every week so you never have to type it again.
Try signing in with the company email.
Skip the dashboard and estimate the numbers.
perguntas.explica: The login is yours. A password written in the sheet or conversation is stored where it shouldn't be. And estimating numbers is prohibited: if it can't find something, it writes "couldn't find".

perguntas.p: What is the "First task" at the end of the sheet for?
opcoes: So the agent remembers what it did last week.
To run it once right away so you can check that the sheet works before trusting it.
To schedule the task on the calendar.
To tell clients, in the very first interaction, that an agent is handling customer service.
perguntas.explica: The first task is the sheet's test: run it now, check it, and correct the sheet if needed. Chat doesn't keep a schedule on its own; scheduling comes later.

perguntas.p: In chat, where does the sheet go so it applies to every conversation with that agent?
opcoes: In a file on your computer that chat finds and reads on its own when needed.
In the history of any other conversation.
In the instructions for a Project (ChatGPT or Claude) or a Gem.
perguntas.explica: Project or Gem instructions apply to every conversation created inside them. Chat doesn't read files on your computer by itself; in the terminal, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the folder does that job.

itens.texto: Role, about me, when, steps, rules, delivery, and first task. One line each.
Read only, draft only, login is yours, money goes through you. And exact numbers or "couldn't find".
In chat, in the Project or Gem instructions; in the terminal, in the folder’s AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
